title: Answer a bad address from the middleware chain, before any order is stored
description: A bad address used to get as far as `createOrder`, which checked it first thing and threw, and the JSON middleware turned the throw into a 400 beside every other malformed body. That put the one check that can refuse an order outright behind the handler's door, and made a postcode we cannot route read like a body-shape error when it is a content one. The check now sits in the chain: `validateAddressBody()` runs after the API key and the JSON parse on POST /orders, hands the handler the normalised address, and answers 422 with the field that failed, so a request with an address the shop cannot ship to is turned away before an order exists for it and before the gateway is asked. `createOrder` takes the address as already checked and no longer calls `validateAddress`; json.ts stops mapping `AddressError`, since nothing past the middleware throws it. The storefront sees 422 rather than 400 for a bad address, which is the one visible change; a body with no address at all is still the handler's 400, and GET keeps its chain. `isRecord` moves to json.ts so the middleware and the route share it. The new middleware test drives the route through `runChain`, as the webhook tests do, and create's own test for the removed check goes.

commit.subject: Validate the address in middleware, before the handler
commit.body:
validateAddressBody() runs after jsonBody on POST /orders and answers
422 naming the field; createOrder takes the address as checked; json.ts
no longer maps AddressError; isRecord shared from json.ts.
